observation_summary: The compiler flags for warning levels (jscomp_error, jscomp_warning, jscomp_off) do not respect the order in which they are provided on the command line. The system incorrectly prioritizes certain flags over others regardless of their sequence, causing tests that expect the last-provided flag to take precedence to fail.
reasoning_summary: The bug report explicitly states that the current implementation uses a fixed precedence (off > warning > error) instead of allowing the last-provided argument to override previous ones. This is a procedural logic error in how the compiler processes and applies configuration flags. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a simple value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object); it is a flaw in the algorithmic strategy used to resolve flag precedence.
evidence_used: bug_report_description: '"off" always takes precedence over "warning", and "warning" always takes precedence over "error" This should be changed so that the last arguments always has highest precedence.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the flags relate to each other, the core issue is the procedural logic (the algorithm) used to determine the final state of the warning configuration based on the input sequence.
The issue is not about initializing a single variable incorrectly, but about the logic used to process a sequence of inputs to determine a final state.
